transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I’m here because since we put in a brighter mirror in the bathroom, I keep noticing the skin around my cheeks and jaw. It looks uneven or sort of saggy to me. My husband says he can’t really see it, but I keep seeing it.
Do you find yourself checking your face in mirrors over and over because of this?

Most mornings, yes. I’ll look at my face from a few different angles and put on extra makeup before I leave for the courthouse. I also catch myself comparing my face to women at work, and sometimes I avoid casual pictures if I’m not feeling good about how I look.
How much is this worry about your face interfering with your daily life?

I still get my work done, but getting ready takes extra time. I’ve rushed into the courthouse a few mornings, and I’ve missed the start of yoga more than once. I’ve also skipped some casual photos at book club or community events because I didn’t want to worry about how my face would look.
When you think about your cheeks and jaw, does it feel like there is something actually wrong with how your face looks?
Yes, it does to me. The skin around my cheeks and jaw just looks uneven, or kind of saggy, especially since we got that brighter mirror. My husband says he doesn’t see it, but I can see it.
Do you think you might be overestimating how noticeable this looks to other people?
Maybe. My husband keeps telling me he can’t really see it, but in that brighter mirror the skin around my cheeks and jaw looks uneven and kind of saggy to me. It’s hard for me not to notice it.
On a typical day, about how much total time do you spend thinking about how your cheeks and jaw look?

It’s not all day, but I do find myself thinking about it several times—especially when I’m in the bathroom mirror. Ever since we put in that brighter mirror, I keep noticing the skin around my cheeks and jaw and wondering if it looks uneven or saggy.
Do you get unwanted, repetitive thoughts about your cheeks and jaw that feel intrusive and hard to resist?

Yes, they do keep coming back. Since we put in that brighter mirror, I notice my cheeks and jaw and start thinking the skin looks uneven or saggy. I know my husband says he doesn’t see it, but it’s hard for me to just let the thought go.
When the thought about your cheeks and jaw comes up, do you do anything over and over to feel less anxious about it?

Most mornings I check my face from a few different angles, and I usually put on a little extra makeup before I leave for the courthouse. Sometimes I compare myself to women at work, too, or avoid casual pictures if I’m feeling bad about how it looks.
Do you think the problem with your cheeks and jaw is definitely real, or is it possible your mind is exaggerating it?

I mean, it looks real to me when I see it in that brighter mirror—the skin around my cheeks and jaw just seems uneven or saggy. But my husband honestly says he can’t see what I’m talking about, so... I guess it’s possible I’m making it bigger in my mind.
On most days, do these worries about your cheeks and jaw take up more than an hour of your time in total?
I’m not really sure. I do check in the morning and sometimes think about it at work, but I haven’t kept track of how long it adds up to.
How upset do these worries about your cheeks and jaw make you?

It upsets me some, but I still get my work done. I do spend extra time getting ready, though, and that’s made me rush into the courthouse a few mornings. I’ve missed the start of yoga more than once, and I’ve skipped a few casual photos at book club or community things because I didn’t want to worry about how my face looked.
Besides your cheeks and jaw, do you also get preoccupied with how any other part of your body looks?

No, it’s mainly my cheeks and jaw. Ever since that brighter bathroom mirror went in, I keep noticing the skin there looking uneven or kind of saggy, even though my husband says he really can’t see it.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days?
I’m not sure I’d say depressed most days. I get frustrated and self-conscious about my face, but I’m still going to work and doing my usual things.
Do you have similar intrusive thoughts and repeated checking or reassurance-seeking about things other than your appearance?
No, I haven’t really noticed that with other things. It’s mostly just my appearance.
On most days, do thoughts about your cheeks and jaw take up more than an hour in total?
No, I don’t think it adds up to more than an hour most days. I notice it when I’m in the bathroom mirror, especially since it’s so bright, and it bothers me, but it’s not constant all day.
Do you worry a lot about many other things in your life besides how your cheeks and jaw look?
I’m not really sure what you mean by “a lot.” I have normal things to deal with, but I haven’t noticed myself worrying about lots of different things the same way I do about my face.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient is preoccupied with a perceived defect in appearance (cheeks/jaw looking uneven or saggy) that others do not observe, and performs repetitive appearance-related behaviors including mirror checking, angle checking, extra makeup use, comparison with others, and photo avoidance. The concern causes distress and mild functional interference. OCD-spectrum symptoms are limited to appearance concerns, supporting body dysmorphic disorder rather than another specified OCD. However, the interview does not clearly establish the DSM/ICD time threshold of typically >1 hour/day, so F45.22 remains the best fit among the listed candidates but with relatively mild/subthreshold severity.
